stop_condition: Done when (1) the widened Section 1S discovery is verified EMPIRICALLY to cover what its header claims - each category count and the union reproduced by an independent enumeration, and each of the six OUT-of-scope carve-outs probed for whether its 'proven absent' assertion can actually fail; (2) the 1SM pairing control is confirmed to RUN the shipped discovery rather than simulate it; (3) the shipped operator block is rendered from real bytes and read for the corrected threat model; (4) the fkm.10 reviewer-row change is checked for internal consistency against model-select's role-to-agent mapping. Then either a finding at or above high, or verdict=approve. Bounded: no fifth/sixth guard shape is proposed; documentation-honesty fixes only.

findings.evidence: Line 738-739 asserts of the 90-file union: 'This is what an operator actually reads or the plugin actually ships.' Line 133-134 asserts 'Section 1S's own header states the full in/out partition.' Both are measurably false. MEASURED: `bash .claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh generate "$PWD" | wc -l` = 138 shipped-surface rows (the repo's OWN declaration of what it ships, the same instrument qa.md section 10 cites as the oracle for a project-declared surface). Subtracting the spec's union (110 rows absent), then filtering to prose/script files, leaves 35 shipped paths that are in NEITHER the IN list NOR the OUT list: 19 .claude/scripts/*.sh (impact-report.sh, escalation-basis via beads-ledger.sh, lessons.sh, model-select.sh, tech-debt.sh, epic-gate.sh, codex-review.sh, codex-detect.sh, workflow-denylist.sh, workflow-doctor.sh, workflow-manifest.sh, workflow-model-apply.sh, current-task.sh, detect-stack.sh, statusline.sh, tree-lease.sh, worktree-sweep.sh, resolve-fixture-spec.sh, beads-quarantine.sh), 6 .claude/rubrics/*.md, .claude/settings.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .mcp.json, 2 .claude/mcp/*/README.md, grammars/MANIFEST.md, 2 .claude/vendor/superpowers/*.md. install.sh:757 states 'the rest of .claude/scripts/*.sh rides the glob copy below', and install.sh:2659-2662 copies .claude/rubrics/*.md, so all 25 of those ARE installed into an operator's tree. The six rubrics carry manifest class 'operator' verbatim: `workflow-manifest.sh generate "$PWD" | grep '^.claude/rubrics/'` prints six rows whose class column reads 'operator'. The OUT paragraph at :629-635 gives only one rationale ('because they are archives and rewriting them would be its own dishonesty'), which cannot cover a shipped executable script or an operator-class rubric, so those 35 are not merely unlisted - they are outside the stated partition's own logic. Section 4 states its coverage residual explicitly (:1485-1533, naming R4-F1); Section 1S states none: `grep -niE 'residual|not covered|does not (cover|scan)' <spec>` returns hits only in Section 4's headers and the archives paragraph.
findings.description: The round-6 deliverable reproduces, in its own documentation, the exact defect it was dispatched to fix. The orchestrator's finding of 2026-09-06T17:57:25Z named the root cause as 'a check that is real, correct, and called, with an INPUT SET narrower than the claim it licenses' - which reads as 'no banned claim ships' and means 'not in these 16 files'. The widened scan now reads as 'this is what the plugin actually ships' and means 'these 90 of 138 declared rows'. That is the same sentence-shape as R5-F1 ('THE FULL CONTRIBUTOR SET, verified by reading the call graph' over a list missing one contributor), which was rated HIGH and blocked one round ago in this same file; here the omission is 35 paths, six of them classed 'operator' by the repo's own manifest. It is a latent gap, not a live one: my whole-tree sweep with the shipped normalizer found ZERO illegitimate hits in any unscanned file (every hit outside archives is the 'proof that' false-positive class - see R6-F4). The harm is the sentence, which tells the next maintainer the surface is covered and stops them looking - precisely how HANDOFF.md carried the claim through four review rounds. REQUIRED FIX, prose-only and proven pin-neutral (adding a header comment to a scratch copy still yields 179 passed / 0 failed): (a) replace :738-739 with a claim that matches the set, e.g. 'this is the subset of the shipped surface this scan covers'; (b) drop or qualify 'the full in/out partition' at :133-134; (c) add a STATED COVERAGE RESIDUAL to Section 1S's header in the same form Section 4 already uses, naming the third category (~35 shipped prose/script paths, including .claude/scripts/*.sh and the operator-class .claude/rubrics/*.md) and why it was left out this round. NOT REQUIRED and explicitly not asked for: widening the scan or building another guard shape - the operator ruled 'accept and document the residual, ship', and this finding asks for exactly the documenting half of that ruling. SEPARATE, LOW, same edit: the arithmetic at :735-736 ('24+8+8+39+4+9+24 = 116 raw, minus 10 overlaps = 106...') double-counts qa-gate.sh and verify-before-stop.sh; the five categories sum to 100 and 100-10 = 90, which is the asserted value.

findings.evidence: The header at :753-754 states: 'A leak here (e.g. a bug in the docs/reviews/** exclusion filter) would mean the positive allowlist claim above is not actually what runs.' MEASURED: I removed the exclusion outright in a scratchpad copy - discover_docs_md became `find "$root/docs" -name '*.md' 2>/dev/null | sort -u`, printed to confirm the mutation landed - and ran it: '179 passed, 0 failed', exit 0, zero FAIL lines. 1S.12.4 cannot fail for that bug by construction: discover_docs_md matches only -name '*.md', and `find docs/reviews -type f | sed 's#.*\.##' | sort | uniq -c` = 72 json, 0 md, so the exclusion can never change the result and the carve-out example chosen to guard it is a .json path no .md-only discovery could return. CONTRAST, so the finding is scoped and not overstated: the other carve-outs ARE sensitive. Adding CHANGELOG.md to discover_named_root_files fails 1S.12.1 (plus 1S.4/1S.5/1S.10/1S.11/1SM.4, 173 passed / 6 failed); widening discover_docs_md to `find "$root"` fails 1S.12.1 AND 1S.12.2 (172 passed / 7 failed).
findings.description: An assertion whose header names a specific bug class it would catch, and which structurally cannot catch it. Same family as R5-F2 (assert_absent invoked but never defined) one round earlier in this file: a check that claims to check. Severity is MEDIUM not HIGH because no coverage is actually lost - the DANGEROUS direction (an exclusion that is too broad, silently shrinking the scanned set) is caught by 1S.2's exact count, and the direction the mutation exercises (exclusion too narrow) only adds archives and would fail loudly on content. The defect is the header's claim about which assertion covers what. FIX, either: (a) reword :753-754 to say these are absence facts about the current discovery rather than filter guards, or (b) make it real for ~5 lines in the 1SM style - seed a sandbox docs/reviews/seeded.md carrying the banned phrase, assert discover_docs_md excludes it, restore control on the real tree. (b) is preferable and costs one sandbox leg, not a new mechanism.

findings.evidence: The exact-count assertions pin a CARDINALITY, not a SET, so a compensating drop-plus-add is invisible. MEASURED: in a scratchpad copy I made discover_docs_md drop docs/HOOKS.md (`| grep -v '/docs/HOOKS.md$'`) and add .claude/rubrics/default.md, keeping the count at 39 and the union at 90. Result: '179 passed, 0 failed', exit 0, zero FAIL lines - with docs/HOOKS.md, one of the two files THIS ROUND had to correct, silently outside the scanned set. My independent enumeration confirms the shipped counts are right today: script mirrors 8/8/8, docs 39, named root 4, agents 9, plugin-installed 24, union 90 (`find`-based recomputation plus a direct run of the shipped discovery functions), so this is a hole in the guard, not a wrong number.
findings.description: ANSWER TO THE EXACT-VS-FLOOR QUESTION THE SPECIALIST RAISED, stated as a recommendation: KEEP EXACT, DO NOT GO TO FLOORS, and upgrade the two organically-growing categories plus the union from exact-COUNT to exact-SET. Floors are the wrong trade here because 'we scanned at least N' is the same shape as the defect this task exists to fix - the 16-file scan would have satisfied any floor, and the failure mode floors cannot see (a silent shrink from 39 to 30) is the only one that matters. Exact counts are strictly better than floors and catch the silent zero, the silent shrink and the silent widening; the churn cost is a loud one-digit edit with the re-measure command already printed beside it, which is the convention EXPECTED_SPECS already runs on in this repo. But exact counts admit the compensating error demonstrated above, at zero additional maintenance cost to close: pin a sorted list of project-relative paths (or its sha256) for docs/**/*.md, plugin-installed and the union, and the failure message then names WHICH file appeared or disappeared instead of only that a number moved. Keep plain exact counts for the closed categories (8 mirrors, 4 named root, 9 agents), where a set pin adds nothing.

findings.evidence: The round-6 notes and the spec header at :650-654 classify the review-check.sh:2556 rewrite as 'one INCIDENTAL false-positive collision'. It is systematic, not incidental. MEASURED with the shipped normalizer over the whole tree, the 'proof that' alternative matches ordinary English in nine files with no relation to any forgery claim: .claude/scripts/codex-review.sh:550, .claude/tests/README.md:403, .claude/tests/component/specs/denylist-shared.sh:898, .claude/scripts/tests/workflow-doctor.test.sh:622, .claude/scripts/tests/design-gate-precheck-wiring.test.sh:459, .claude/scripts/tests/design-conform.test.sh:745, .claude/tests/e2e/specs/multi-domain-signup.spec.ts:93, .claude/tests/e2e/specs/_fixture-restore.unit.spec.ts:178, CHANGELOG.md:2572. None is inside the 90 today (I confirmed the union is at 0 hits under the full shipped pattern), but docs/**/*.md and .claude/agents/*.md are prose-heavy and now in scope, so recurrence is structural. The alternative also carries no unique detection value: re-running the spec's own five positive-detection strings (1M.a-d plus the seeded HANDOFF line) against the pattern with 'proof that' removed gives a match on all five, because each is caught by tamper-evident / tamper evident / unforgeable.
findings.description: JUDGMENT ON THE REWORD, since it was raised for review: the reword itself is correct and I verified it is semantically null and non-executable - 'the tested proof that property must survive' to 'the tests proving this property must survive' in a comment, with `git diff` showing zero non-comment change in review-check.sh. Disclosing it in the header rather than hiding it is right. What is wrong is calling it INCIDENTAL, because that framing licenses the next reviewer to reword again rather than fix the matcher, and in a repo whose thesis is that documentation must be honest, a matcher that makes maintainers edit honest prose to go green is a bad incentive to install - the next reword may not be semantically null. RECOMMENDATION: drop 'proof that' from BANNED_CLAIM_PATTERN and say why in the same comment. This is NOT the 'maintaining the denylist' mistake the file header forbids - that warning is about EXTENDING the alternation believing it is the guard; the pattern is documented as a readable DIAGNOSTIC (2P is load-bearing), and a false positive is the exact opposite of a readable failure. If it is kept instead, then the header must record the false-positive CLASS with the reword recipe, not a one-off.
